newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt ends mixed, Brazil fears wane.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt ends mixed, Brazil fears wane.

text.p: Brady prices were mostly mixed in lackadaisical trade on Monday, settling down from fears last week about possible currency pressures surfacing on the Brazilian real, traders said.
Concerns over the outlook for Brazil faded, and dealers held vigil for the testimony of Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan before Congress on Tuesday.
"It looks like today there has been a dissipation of the pressures of Brazil," said Peter Allen, head of emerging market research at BankBoston Securities.
Last week, the Brady market had slipped amid talk that Brazil might be next in line -- following some Asian countries -- to devalue its currency, widely believed to be overvalued by up to 25 percent.
But investor skittishness seemed to wane after the Brazilian Central Bank reaffirmed that no currency devaluation was in the works.
On Monday, Brazil Brady spreads over Treasuries were several basis points wider in morning trade, but that gap narrowed later in the session, said one trader.
"They caught a little bit of a bid, but we can't really attribute it to customer buying," he said.
Brazil's "C" bonds were unchanged at 81-3/8 bid, while its par bonds were off 1/8 at 69-3/8 bid.
Overall, customer volume was light and yield spreads to Treasuries were largely mixed, give or take a few basis points, traders said.
"It's been very quiet. One asset hasn't tremendously outperformed another," said one trader at a large U.S. investment bank.
Activity was largely sidelined ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's two-day testimony on monetary policy before Congress, known as the Humphrey-Hawkins hearing, he said.
"We didn't expect to see much today before the Humphrey-Hawkins speech," the trader said.
Among other Latin American debt, Mexico's liquid global bond due 2026 slipped 1/8 at 117-1/8 bid.
Meanwhile, in Eastern European Brady instruments, Russian and Bulgarian spreads tightened by a whisker, traders said.
